profile.headline: Lead Software Engineer
profile.summary:
After completing a PhD in Physics focused on nonlinear dynamics, I moved into software and infrastructure engineering to continue working on what has always interested me most: understanding and building complex systems.
 
I’m currently a Lead Software Engineer at Arcules / Milestone Systems, where much of my recent work has focused on production AI systems and modern software architecture. I lead development of an agentic AI system that enables users to interact dynamically with their data using LLMs, tool calling, retrieval, memory, guardrails, and evaluation.
 
I’ve also designed a fine-tuned local LLM moderation service, led LLM-assisted security red-team efforts, helped introduce AI-assisted code and merge-request review workflows, and contributed to the architecture and implementation of our data lakehouse.
 
My broader background spans distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, security, data engineering, and production reliability. I’m particularly interested in the engineering required to turn probabilistic AI systems into dependable software.

positions.title: Research Assistant, Teaching Assistant, Graduate Student
positions.description:
Research assistant under three year NSF grant PHY-0754081 working with Dr. Robert Gilmore.  This grant was a combination research and outreach grant under which I was the primary graduate student.  Research resulted in new insights into how the shape of Strange Attractors are baked into the governing dynamical equations, and the discovery of a new mechanism which is responsible for a previous discovery of periodicity transitions spirals in the codimension-2 parameter plane of Smale-like strange attractors.  


As part of the outreach component of this grant, developed the iOS app Chaos Lab:  http://itunes.apple.com/us/app/chaos-lab/id398270047; developed a Braille and Embossed-Figure based introductory booklet about Chaos Theory for visually-impaired students, and produced a series of cinematic visualizations of strange attractors (http://www.youtube.com/tdj2828), including the short film Bachaos presented at a recent conference in France
(http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OvNkEid1LsA).

positions.title: System Administrator, Department of Physics
positions.description: Duties include maintaining and upgrading department computers, including three e-mail servers, one web server, one NFS file server, one NIS server, and fifteen workstations. Under my tenure I have enthusiastically modernized our computer systems, including overseeing major computer purchases (terabyte sized servers and fast workstations) and upgrading to Debian Ubuntu (workstations) distributions of Linux. I’ve also introduced a department mailing list for the first time, web-mail, and a wiki for students to share their Linux experience. I have lesser experience with an OpenBSD NAT server and mail server.

positions.title: Freelance System Administration and Web Design
positions.description:
Various work includes Linux system administration for a local Dental Group, and Web design (including html,css,php) for Greater Philadelphia Chinese STARTALK Academy, North Laurel Elementary School (Laurel, Delaware)
